findings.title: VMPR sheep/goat-feed exception is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: it is always necessary to add one of the four codes grouped under the A07VF code.
findings.observation: The feed guidance allows implicit F23 but omits the specific requirement to refine implicit Sheep and goat feed (A07VF) with a child descriptor.
findings.action: Add the scoped exception. Verify child codes against the catalogue: the source prints A18EX for two different goat labels, so do not copy that list blindly.
findings.resolution: Added the explicit child requirement; all four targcon children verified in local MTX 17.2. A18EY corrects the duplicated goat label in the PDF.

resolution_evidence.quote: A feed term with implicit `F23.A07VF Sheep and goat feed` needs an explicit child descriptor: `A18ET` lambs reared for reproduction or meat production, `A18EV` dairy/reproductive sheep, `A18EX` kids reared for reproduction or meat production, or `A18EY` dairy/reproductive goats, according to the known target. The broader implicit sheep/goat facet alone is insufficient for this specific VMPR case. Do not guess the species or production purpose. (ChemMon 2026 p36; child labels and `targcon` membership checked in local MTX 17.2)

findings.title: VMPR edible-casing instructions are absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: For edible casings, the base term to be used is A0F1J. When including the source, the source commodity (F27 facet) must be manually inserted.
findings.observation: The mapping page mentions Casings as an output but the coding overlay does not explain the A0F1J base and explicit F27 source-commodity instruction.
findings.action: Add the coding boundary and a catalogue-checked example, using the adult-sheep example on page 37 as source evidence.
findings.resolution: Added casing base/F27 guidance and the adult-sheep example; code identities and memberships checked in MTX 17.2.

resolution_evidence.quote: In VMPR reporting, use `A0F1J Edible casings` for edible casings. When including the source commodity, insert the appropriate `F27` explicitly; the generic casing base does not supply that source commodity. Keep this food matrix separate from the non-food `A0C60` convention. (ChemMon 2026 p36)

findings.title: Additives F03 recommendation has lost its category scope
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: The physical-state facet (F03) should be considered for samples belonging to the following legislative food categories/subcategories:
findings.observation: The wiki says F03 is highly recommended in several categories but never identifies those categories; the source lists 1, 6.3, 12.5, 12.6, 13, 14.1.2-14.1.5 and 17.
findings.action: Include the category list from page 38 and the page-39 condition that F03 is added when not implicit. Preserve recommendation strength rather than making it a universal requirement.
findings.resolution: Added all ten source-listed category rows and retained highly recommended/when-not-implicit scope; corrected the validation summary.

resolution_evidence.quote: `F03 Physical-state` should be considered for the following legislative categories and is highly recommended when not already implicit. This is a scoped recommendation, not a universal mandatory facet. (ChemMon 2026 p38-39)

findings.title: Arsenic-specific rice and algae guidance is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: Reporting of rice-based products. If a product contains rice (e.g. a ready-to-eat meal for children, cereal-based; rice cake) it should be specified in this field.
findings.observation: The contaminants overlay omits Table 8 recommendations for rice processing/dehydration (F28, CHEMON18), rice ingredients (F04), and algae identification; generic process and ingredient guidance does not explain these triggers.
findings.action: Add a conditional arsenic entry using pages 95-96, including rice type and Hijiki detail. Keep these as recommendations for this domain.
findings.resolution: Added rice processing/dehydration, ingredient, rice-type and algae/Hijiki recommendations under an arsenic-specific scope.

resolution_evidence.quote: | Arsenic and derivatives: rice grains for human consumption | `F28` should distinguish unprocessed from processed rice; describe known treatment and whether the sample is dehydrated. Preserve the type of rice. | ChemMon 2026 Table 8 p95-96, CHEMON18 |

findings.title: Chlorate/perchlorate process recommendation is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: Therefore, it is recommended to report facet F28 (Process) and select at least the code for ‘processed’ or ‘unprocessed’; if possible, specify the most appropriate code describing the process from the SSD2 catalogue
findings.observation: No wiki page explains the CHEMON19 recommendation to report F28 processed/unprocessed, or a more specific known treatment, for chlorates and perchlorates.
findings.action: Add the Table 8 conditional F28 recommendation without inventing processing details or applying it to unrelated contaminant cases.
findings.resolution: Added CHEMON19 process recommendation with known-information and facet-legality constraints.

resolution_evidence.quote: | Chlorates and perchlorates | Report `F28` with at least processed/unprocessed information, or the most appropriate known treatment, such as blanching or deep-freezing. | ChemMon 2026 Table 8 p97, CHEMON19 |

findings.title: PAH packaging-material recommendation is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: It is recommended to describe the container or wrapper that holds the product as marketed.
findings.observation: The wiki covers F19 for bisphenols/phthalates and general packaging but omits polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), the CHEMON15 recommendation, and its marketed-package scope.
findings.action: Add the PAH-specific F19 recommendation. Distinguish marketed packaging from the sample container used during analysis.
findings.resolution: Added CHEMON15 marketed-package F19 recommendation and a matching packaging-page explanation separating lab containers.

resolution_evidence.quote: | Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) | Report `F19` for the material of the container or wrapper holding the product as marketed. The laboratory sample container is a separate matter. See [[packaging-facets]]. | ChemMon 2026 Table 8 p93, CHEMON15 |

findings.title: Acrylamide ingredient recommendation is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: It is recommended that the list of ingredients is provided in the ‘Ingredients’ facet for the following food items:
findings.observation: The wiki retains mandatory acrylamide F33 but omits the separate recommended F04 detail for potato crisps, pre-cooked fries/home potato products, breakfast cereals excluding muesli/porridge, dry substitute coffee and specified baby foods.
findings.action: Add the source-listed product groups and recommended ingredient detail as a scoped overlay; reconcile with normal ingredient rules rather than generalising it to every food.
findings.resolution: Added the exact product-group ingredient recommendation and ingredient-page explanation; mandatory F33 and normal source/ingredient legality retained.

resolution_evidence.quote: | Acrylamide: potato crisps; pre-cooked French fries/potato products for home cooking; breakfast cereals excluding muesli and porridge; dry substitute coffee; baby foods other than processed cereal-based foods | Provide ingredient detail in `F04` for these listed groups, in addition to the required `F33`. See [[ingredient-facets]] for ingredient-versus-source legality. | ChemMon 2026 Table 8 p91 |

findings.title: Mycotoxin production-method recommendation is absent
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2026 - Chemical monitoring reporting guidance  2026 data collection.pdf

findings.resolution: Added CHEMON17 organic/non-organic F21 recommendation for known information; retained recommended rather than mandatory status.

findings.title: Dismissed and deprecated terms are not distinguished accurately
findings.source_excerpt: Dismissed terms are made not reportable in one or more hierarchies of the FoodEx2 catalogue, but they continue to be reportable in others
findings.observation: The maintenance page mentions dismissal in some hierarchies, while validation guidance says deprecated and dismissed terms are always invalid without explaining the hierarchy scope. The source distinguishes dismissal from all-hierarchy deprecation.
findings.action: Explain the distinction and reconcile BR21 wording with the validator reporting hierarchy. Do not weaken validation based on this historical definition alone.
findings.resolution: Clarified dismissal versus deprecation across rule, validation, ChemMon and maintenance pages; inspected sibling mapping and BR21 implementation, retaining blocking results.

resolution_evidence.quote: Rule: a `BR21` dismissal result remains a blocking error. EFSA distinguishes dismissal in one or more hierarchies from deprecation in all hierarchies: a term dismissed in one hierarchy can remain reportable in another. Always check the intended reporting hierarchy rather than interpreting dismissal as universal catalogue deletion. (Maintenance 2020 p3, footnotes 1-2)

findings.title: Corex vocabulary is missing from the overview
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2015 -  - The food classification and description system FoodEx 2  revision 2.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: The type of term in the basic food list is recorded by the ‘Corex’ attribute.
findings.observation: The wiki mentions core/extended/generic terms but does not define Corex or map H/C/E/M/P to their meanings and coding roles (Table 12, pages 24-25).
findings.action: Add a compact attribute reference, separate from food-nature/type terminology, with the source meanings and the recommended core-or-more-specific coding level.
findings.resolution: Added H/C/E/M/P roles, core-or-more-specific recommendation, food-nature distinction and hierarchy reportability caveat; linked selection guidance.

resolution_evidence.quote: `Corex` records the role/detail class of a food-list term. It is distinct from the food's nature (raw commodity, derivative or composite); a detailed term can still describe any of those natures.

findings.title: Facet reference omits F08, F12 and F22
findings.observation: The facet-category reference omits sweetening agent (F08), dough/mass (F12), and preparation/production place (F22), although source Table 8 lists them; F22 appears only in cardinality rules elsewhere.
findings.action: Add the three category meanings using revision-2 Table 25 (page 47) and maintenance Table 8. Check current catalogue membership before adding descriptor-code examples.
findings.resolution: Added F08 sweetening agent, F12 dough/mass and F22 preparation/production place meanings; no unverified descriptor codes introduced.

resolution_evidence.quote: | `F08` | Sweetening agent | Non-sugar sweetener used in a sweetened product, when known and relevant. |

findings.title: Physical-division rule was reduced to a process code list
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2015 -  - The food classification and description system FoodEx 2  revision 2.pdf
findings.source_excerpt: Examples of processes normally directly applied to the raw commodity; specific derivative groups have generally not been created for them
findings.observation: The wiki listed A07LA but did not clearly retain its ordinary application to raw commodities or distinguish grain milling with separation. The coding-context projection removed the appendix containing the code.
findings.action: Restore the general rule and derivative exceptions in a normal prompt-visible section.
findings.resolution: Restore the general rule and derivative exceptions in a normal prompt-visible section. Source interpretation and limits are recorded in the repair review.

resolution_evidence.quote: Physical division or size reduction does not automatically require a derivative base.

findings.title: BR13 rejection incorrectly prescribed a derivative base
findings.source: foodex2_docs/EFSA Supporting Publications - 2015 -  - The food classification and description system FoodEx 2  revision 2.pdf
findings.locator: p43-44 Table 22, read with official Catalogue Browser BR13
findings.observation: The worked example and related BR13 summary treated F03 rejection as requiring a derivative; SEL-0036 repeated the inference.
findings.action: Separate facet legality from food classification, preserve the known-permitted-grinding path and repair the evaluation rubric.
findings.resolution: Separate facet legality from food classification, preserve the known-permitted-grinding path and repair the evaluation rubric. Source interpretation and limits are recorded in the repair review.

resolution_evidence.quote: A `BR13` rejection identifies an invalid raw-base/F03 combination; it does not determine the correct base-term class.

resolution_review: All 11 scoped findings checked against the revised wiki and the cited source passages; local catalogue/validator checks in reports/source-coverage/2026-09-30-catalogue-check.json. No exhaustive corpus claim.
